To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) event joins in different domains are all variants of the same computation, 2) this can be uniformly expressed in terms of effect handlers, 3) the resulting design is extensible and modular, 4) it can be efficiently implemented on multicore processors.

(1) we present the first language to uniformly express variants from the domains of event processing, reactive programming, concurrent programming, and stream-relational algebra; and (2) we present a formal semantics and prototypes in Koa and multicore OCAML.

(1) we have designed a language with a uniform, extensible and efficient way to express n-way joins over event streams; (2) the design is based on algebraic effects and effect handlers; (3) we have implemented a prototype in Koka and OCaml; (4) we have validated the performance of our design with a set of microbenchmarks.
